title: Meroke Preserve: A Name in the Wetlands
summary: Meroke Preserve carries a Native regional name into a protected wetland landscape along Newbridge Creek in Bellmore.
address_label: Meroke Preserve, Orange and Farmer streets, Bellmore
ancestral_territory_note: The preserve carries a historical form of the Merrick name.
why_this_matters: Meroke remains part of the everyday geography of the South Shore. Connecting the name with a protected creek landscape invites people to learn its history while caring for the place that now carries it.
introduction_content: Meroke Preserve, also listed by Nassau County as Merokee Preserve, protects about 25 acres of woods and wetlands between Sunrise Highway and Merrick Road. Newbridge Creek divides into two channels through the preserve.
history_content:
Meroke is one of the historical forms of the Merrick name. Today it names a quiet stretch of woods and wetlands along Newbridge Creek in Bellmore.

Robert S. Grumet includes the preserve in the Merrick entry of his place-name history, Beyond Manhattan.
whereintheworld_content: The preserve is at Orange and Farmer streets in Bellmore, between Sunrise Highway and Merrick Road. Follow designated trails through the woods and wetlands.
